skill.name: webapp-nikto
skill.description: Guides authorized Nikto scans to identify web server vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, exposed files, outdated software, and weak security controls.
skill.summary: Plan, run, interpret, and document authorized Nikto web server assessments.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, reserved example URLs, defensive samples, and standard local report processing. The CI template executes an unverified remote installer and uses mutable third-party actions in security-sensitive workflows. The skill also provides actionable IDS and WAF evasion guidance despite repeated authorization warnings.

remediation.issue: A remote script is piped directly into Bash from a mutable branch.
remediation.suggestion: Download a versioned release, verify its checksum or signature, and execute only the verified local file.

remediation.issue: Third-party GitHub Actions use mutable release tags or the master branch.
remediation.suggestion: Pin every third-party action to a reviewed commit SHA and use dependency automation for controlled updates.

remediation.issue: The skill provides detailed IDS and WAF evasion commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion guidance, or restrict it to approved validation goals with explicit authorization and monitoring requirements.

remediation.issue: The CI scan example accepts any target URL without an allowlist.
remediation.suggestion: Require an approved target allowlist and reject private, loopback, link-local, metadata, or out-of-scope destinations.

content.value_statement: Web teams need a repeatable way to identify server weaknesses before attackers find them. This skill guides authorized Nikto scans and structured remediation reporting.
actual_capabilities: Builds Nikto commands for scoped hosts, ports, TLS settings, authentication, proxies, tuning options, and time limits.
Guides single-host, multi-port, authenticated, internal, external, and bulk web server assessments.
Explains Nikto tuning categories, plugins, evasion flags, performance controls, and output formats.
Organizes findings by severity, validation status, affected endpoint, and remediation priority.
Provides CI, SIEM, reporting, and defensive monitoring examples for Nikto results.
limitations: Requires Nikto and Perl to be installed in the execution environment.
Cannot confirm authorization, ownership, or legal scope for a target.
Nikto findings can include false positives and require manual validation.
Scanning can generate heavy traffic, affect production systems, and trigger security alerts.

use_cases.title: Assess a staging server
use_cases.description: Plan a focused Nikto scan, review exposed files and configuration findings, and prepare developer remediation tasks.

use_cases.title: Validate server hardening
use_cases.description: Compare authorized scan results before and after patching to confirm that risky server behavior is removed.

use_cases.title: Prepare audit evidence
use_cases.description: Create a scoped assessment record with timestamps, findings, validation notes, and remediation priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an authorized Nikto scan for [target] on [ports]. Confirm scope, propose a low-impact command, and explain each option before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one approved web server

prompt_templates.title: Review scan findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Nikto output: [findings]. Group findings by severity, identify likely false positives, and propose manual validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis of completed scan results

prompt_templates.title: Design authenticated testing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authenticated Nikto assessment for [application] using [approved credential method]. Limit duration and request rate, then define secure report handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing of an approved application

prompt_templates.title: Build a gated CI scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gated CI workflow for authorized Nikto scans against [staging target]. Pin dependencies, validate targets, preserve reports, and fail on defined severity thresholds.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert integration into a controlled delivery pipeline

output_examples.input: Plan a low-impact scan of staging.example.com on HTTPS port 443 during an approved maintenance window.
output: Scope: staging.example.com on port 443 during the approved window.
Approach: start with limited tuning, a short maximum duration, and a pause between requests.
Records: preserve the command, timestamps, operator, result file, and any observed service impact.

output_examples.input: Summarize a Nikto report containing an outdated server banner, missing security headers, and an exposed backup file.
output: High priority: verify the exposed backup file and remove public access immediately.
Medium priority: confirm the server version and apply supported security updates.
Lower priority: add missing security headers after testing application compatibility.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and record approved hosts, ports, credentials, and testing windows before scanning.
Start with narrow tuning and conservative timing, then expand only when scope and server capacity permit.
Validate findings manually and remove credentials or session data before sharing reports.
anti_patterns: Do not scan public, customer, or third-party systems without explicit written permission.
Do not treat every Nikto result as confirmed without reproduction and contextual review.
Do not use evasion options to bypass monitoring, access controls, or scope restrictions.

faq.question: Does this skill install or run Nikto automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflows. Execution requires Nikto, Perl, and explicit approval in the active environment.

faq.question: Can I scan a production server?
faq.answer: Only with written authorization, an approved window, tested rate limits, backups, monitoring, and an emergency contact.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use approved secret storage and temporary accounts. Never place real passwords, API keys, or session cookies in prompts or reports.

faq.question: Are Nikto findings always accurate?
faq.answer: No. Validate each finding manually and consider server configuration, application behavior, and compensating controls before assigning severity.

faq.question: Can Nikto run in CI?
faq.answer: Yes, against approved staging targets. Pin dependencies, validate targets, limit traffic, protect artifacts, and define failure thresholds.

faq.question: What does Nikto not cover?
faq.answer: Nikto focuses on web server checks. It does not replace authenticated application testing, business logic review, code review, or complete compliance validation.
